title: Open enrollment is here: spousal HRA best practices for HR teams
summary: Explore spousal HRA best practices for open enrollment, from configuring your benefits platform to preparing reimbursements and employee support.
body_markdown:
Open enrollment is underway for most of our clients, and it's one of the busiest times of year for Healia's operations team. As enrollment approaches, HR teams come to us with specific questions: Is our enrollment platform set up correctly? What should we tell employees? What happens after enrollment closes? These are the questions we work through with clients every year.


Healia's[Total Care Option](https://healiahealth.com/blog/spousal-hra) (TCO) is a spousal Health Reimbursement Arrangement (HRA) that reimburses eligible healthcare expenses when employees and their families enroll in qualifying coverage through their spouse’s employer's group health plan. By the time enrollment begins, the plan design is typically set. HR's focus shifts to ensuring employees understand the TCO, can elect it correctly, and know where to go with questions.


Here are the spousal HRA best practices our operations team recommends during the weeks around open enrollment. HR teams can use this checklist with their Human Resource Information System (HRIS) administrators, payroll teams, and benefits brokers.


## **Before open enrollment begins: put your enrollment experience to the test**


The enrollment platform is where employees make their coverage elections, so we review the setup with every client before enrollment opens. **We recommend listing the TCO as a $0.00 medical plan option alongside the company's other medical plans** . Employees can compare their options in one place, see that the TCO has no payroll deduction, and avoid accidentally electing both a company medical plan and the TCO.


Keep "Waive coverage" as a separate option from the TCO. Employees who want to participate in the TCO must actively elect it rather than simply declining their employer's medical plan. Although the TCO is an HRA, we recommend against configuring it as one in the benefits administration system because system limitations can create enrollment and reporting issues. Healia provides the benefit description for the enrollment platform, and our account managers review screenshots with the HRIS team to confirm everything is configured correctly before enrollment opens.


## **When enrollment opens: make the DST easy to find**


Employees need a way to compare their household's coverage options before making an election. Healia's[Decision Support Tool](https://healiahealth.com/blog/help-employees-compare-health-plans-open-enrollment) (DST) compares available medical plans, including a spouse's plan, based on estimated total annual healthcare costs. We recommend including the company's DST link in the first open enrollment email and on the benefits portal, along with our[five-minute DST walkthrough](https://vimeo.com/1240433825) . Ideally, the DST is available 2 to 4 weeks before enrollment opens. If that window has passed, sharing it now still gives employees time to compare their options.


Spouses often have the plan documents needed for an accurate comparison, so encourage employees to involve them early. Employees can[invite their spouse to upload plan information](https://healiahealth.com/blog/decision-support-tool-household-coverage-update) directly into the DST or use a similar sample plan for an initial estimate. Enrollment communications should also explain any eligibility requirements specific to the company's TCO, including whether the entire household must move together or whether employees who previously waived coverage qualify.


## **During enrollment: keep household enrollment on track**


Employees who elect the TCO need to add their spouse and any covered dependents in the HRIS. This step is easy to miss, particularly for employees moving their families off the company's medical plan. Missing dependent information is easier to resolve while enrollment is still open, so we recommend including a reminder in the enrollment instructions and any mid-enrollment communications.


We also hear from employees whose spouse has a different open enrollment period. They may want to elect the TCO but aren't sure whether they can join their spouse's plan outside its regular enrollment window. Depending on the circumstances, a qualifying life event or special enrollment right may allow the change. Employees should confirm the rules with their spouse's plan before making an election. Healia's enrollment support team can help them understand their options and what to ask.


## **When enrollment closes: send the first file**


Once enrollment closes, Healia needs the final election information to begin administering the TCO. We use an enrollment file feed to establish eligibility and keep household information current throughout the plan year. The first production file goes to Healia shortly after open enrollment closes. Subsequent files account for new hires, terminations, and dependent changes. Clients without an automated feed can securely upload enrollment information through the Healia dashboard at the start of the plan year and whenever a household is added or removed.


For plans that exclude employees who previously waived coverage, Healia also works with HR and the benefits broker to review the enrollee list. This gives everyone an opportunity to identify eligibility issues and correct elections before the plan year begins.


## **Before the plan year starts: set up reimbursements and ongoing support**


If the TCO includes premium reimbursement, employees submit a paystub so Healia can calculate their monthly reimbursement amount. These reimbursements are generally treated as taxable income, so payroll needs to know how they'll be processed. Depending on the employer's setup, Healia may reimburse employees directly and invoice the company, or payroll may issue reimbursements using amounts Healia provides.


Once the plan year begins, employees contact Healia directly with questions about their TCO coverage, claims, and reimbursements. Our team handles these requests, reducing the time HR spends on day-to-day benefits questions. You can read more about that process in[How Healia's claims process protects HR's time](https://healiahealth.com/blog/how-healias-claims-process-protects-hrs-time) . Healia also calculates TCO COBRA rates for the employer's COBRA vendor and provides the enrollment and coverage data needed for 1095-C reporting.


## **Make open enrollment easier with Healia by your side**


A few checks during open enrollment can prevent problems later. Confirm that the TCO appears correctly in the enrollment platform, give employees access to the DST, check that dependents are included, and send Healia the enrollment file promptly after elections close. Our operations team works with clients throughout this process and takes over employee support once the plan year begins.


If your company already works with Healia, contact your account manager to review any outstanding enrollment questions. Talk to our team about your options.
